original_question: If N is a non-prime II1 factor, determine whether N has a unique sequential commutation orbit.
target_in_paper: Section "Sequential commutation", Problem 27: "Let N be a non-prime II_1 factor. Does it have a unique sequential commutation orbit?"
correct_elements: Your draft already targets the exact open problem in the paper: it has the right ambient object (a non-prime II_1 factor N) and the right property (having a unique sequential commutation orbit). It is very close to the paper's own wording.
missing_details: The orbit in question is an orbit of the sequential commutation equivalence relation on Haar unitaries, not on arbitrary elements or arbitrary unitaries of N.
To make the question stand-alone, one should say what a Haar unitary is (standardly: a unitary u with \tau(u^n)=0 for all n \ge 1).

One should define the sequential commutation relation explicitly: u \sim_N v means there is a finite chain of Haar unitaries in the tracial ultrapower N^\mathcal U connecting u to v, with adjacent terms commuting.
The paper uses a fixed nonprincipal ultrafilter \mathcal U on \mathbb N and the notation N^\mathcal U for the tracial ultrapower; this is implicit in the draft.
“Unique sequential commutation orbit” means exactly one equivalence class under \sim_N among the Haar unitaries of N.
The paper does not impose extra hypotheses here such as separability, Connes embeddability, property Gamma, property (T), or Haagerup property; those would incorrectly broaden or alter the scope.
For full self-containment, “non-prime II_1 factor” should be unpacked as a II_1 factor admitting a nontrivial tensor product decomposition as II_1 factors.
refined_question: Let N be a non-prime II_1 factor, i.e. N admits a nontrivial tensor product decomposition N \cong P \bar\otimes Q into II_1 factors. Fix the paper’s nonprincipal ultrafilter \mathcal U on \mathbb N, and let \sim_N denote the sequential commutation relation on Haar unitaries of N: for Haar unitaries u,v \in N, write u \sim_N v if there exist Haar unitaries w_1,\dots,w_n \in N^\mathcal U such that [u,w_1]=0, [w_k,w_{k+1}]=0 for 1 \le k < n, and [w_n,v]=0. Must \sim_N have exactly one orbit on the Haar unitaries of N?
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper, because it matches Problem 27 in the section "Sequential commutation." The only essential refinements are to make explicit that the relevant equivalence relation is defined on Haar unitaries, that it is formulated via a finite commuting chain in the ultrapower N^\mathcal U, and that no additional assumptions are present in this problem. The nearby paragraph in the same section supplies the hidden notation and scope, while the contrast with Problem 28 shows that separability is not part of Problem 27.
